questions.questionText: Your company hosts a global news website with heavy traffic. Users in Europe are experiencing high latency when loading images stored in a Cloud Storage bucket located in the US. What is the simplest and most cost-effective way to reduce latency for these global users?
options: Enable Cloud CDN on the HTTP(S) Load Balancer in front of the Cloud Storage bucket.
Replicate the Cloud Storage bucket to every Google Cloud region worldwide.
Upgrade the network connection to Cloud Interconnect.
Migrate the images to a Cloud SQL database.
correctAnswers: Enable Cloud CDN on the HTTP(S) Load Balancer in front of the Cloud Storage bucket.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud CDN (Content Delivery Network) uses Google's globally distributed edge points of presence to cache static content (like images) close to the user. This significantly reduces latency and lowers the load on the origin server.

why other options are wrong.Replicate the Cloud Storage bucket to ev: Manually replicating and syncing buckets globally is highly complex, expensive, and unnecessary when Cloud CDN can cache the content automatically at the edge.
why other options are wrong.Upgrade the network connection to Cloud: Cloud Interconnect connects on-premises networks to Google Cloud; it does not improve web application latency for public end-users.
why other options are wrong.Migrate the images to a Cloud SQL databa: Relational databases are not designed for serving static media assets efficiently, and this would increase latency and costs.

questions.questionText: You are designing a high-performance computing (HPC) cluster on Compute Engine. The application requires temporary storage for scratch data with the absolute lowest possible latency and highest IOPS. Which storage type should you attach to your virtual machines?

explanation.general explanation: Local SSDs are physically attached to the server hosting the virtual machine instance. Because they do not traverse the network, they offer the highest IOPS and lowest latency available on Google Cloud, making them ideal for temporary scratch data.

why other options are wrong.SSD Persistent Disk (pd-ssd): While fast, Persistent Disks are network-attached storage. They introduce network latency, making them slower than Local SSDs.
why other options are wrong.Extreme Persistent Disk (pd-extreme): Extreme PDs offer high performance for specific workloads (like SAP HANA), but they are still network-attached and have higher latency than Local SSDs.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage Standard class: Cloud Storage is an object storage service accessed over HTTP. It has much higher latency than block storage and cannot be natively formatted as a high-speed local file system.

questions.questionText: Your application is hosted in the `us-central1` region. Users connecting from Asia are reporting slow network performance. You want to ensure user traffic enters Google's high-performance global network as close to the user as possible. Which network tier should you use?

explanation.general explanation: The Premium Network Tier routes inbound and outbound traffic over Google's global fiber network. Traffic enters Google's network at an edge point of presence (PoP) closest to the user, providing the lowest latency and highest performance.

why other options are wrong.Standard Network Tier: The Standard Network Tier routes traffic over the public internet and only enters Google's network at the PoP closest to the GCP region where the application is hosted, resulting in higher latency.
why other options are wrong.Enterprise Network Tier: There is no 'Enterprise Network Tier' in Google Cloud networking.
why other options are wrong.Global Network Tier: There is no 'Global Network Tier'. The correct terminology is Premium or Standard.

questions.questionText: A monolithic e-commerce application uses Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL. During sales events, the database is overwhelmed by thousands of identical read queries checking product catalog details, causing severe latency. What is the most effective architectural change to improve read latency?
options: Introduce Memorystore for Redis to cache frequent product catalog queries.
Change the Cloud SQL storage type from SSD to HDD.
Migrate the product catalog directly into Cloud Storage.
Upgrade the Cloud SQL instance to use a globally distributed multi-region setup.
correctAnswers: Introduce Memorystore for Redis to cache frequent product catalog queries.

explanation.general explanation: Memorystore for Redis provides sub-millisecond data access. By caching the results of frequent, repetitive read queries in memory, you offload the processing from the Cloud SQL database, drastically reducing latency and freeing up database capacity.

why other options are wrong.Change the Cloud SQL storage type from S: HDDs are slower than SSDs. This would significantly worsen database latency.
why other options are wrong.Migrate the product catalog directly int: Cloud Storage is an object store, not designed for low-latency relational database lookups.
why other options are wrong.Upgrade the Cloud SQL instance to use a: While multi-region is good for disaster recovery, caching is the appropriate solution for identical, repetitive read queries overloading a database.

questions.questionText: You are building an Internet of Things (IoT) application that ingests millions of sensor readings per second. You need a database that provides high throughput and consistent sub-millisecond latency for massive amounts of time-series data. Which database service is designed for this?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Bigtable is a sparsely populated, wide-column NoSQL database. It is heavily optimized for extremely high write and read throughput with consistent sub-millisecond latency, making it the standard Google Cloud choice for IoT and time-series data.

why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL: Cloud SQL is a relational database. It is not designed to scale to millions of writes per second seamlessly.
why other options are wrong.Firestore: Firestore is a NoSQL document database optimized for mobile and web apps, not for the sheer ingestion volume and sub-millisecond latency required by massive IoT sensor streams.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Spanner: While Spanner scales horizontally and provides high availability, it is a relational database optimized for strong consistency, not the ultra-high throughput unstructured time-series ingestion Bigtable excels at.

questions.questionText: Your application has backend instances deployed in multiple Google Cloud regions (e.g., US, Europe, and Asia). You want to ensure that user requests are automatically routed to the closest healthy backend region to minimize latency, using a single Anycast IP address. Which load balancer should you use?

explanation.general explanation: The Global External Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 and uses a single Anycast IP address to route traffic globally. It automatically directs client requests to the closest healthy region, effectively minimizing geographic network latency.

why other options are wrong.Regional External Application Load Balan: Regional load balancers can only distribute traffic to backends within a single region, so they cannot perform proximity-based global routing.
why other options are wrong.Internal TCP/UDP Load Balancer: This is an internal load balancer used for traffic within a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), not for external global user traffic.
why other options are wrong.Regional Internal Application Load Balan: This is for internal HTTP(S) traffic within a single region.

questions.questionText: A corporate reporting tool generates heavy analytical queries against the primary Cloud SQL for MySQL transaction database, slowing down live customer transactions. How can you improve performance and latency for both the customer application and the reporting tool?
options: Create a Cloud SQL Read Replica and point the reporting tool to the replica.
Move the reporting tool to a different Google Cloud zone.
Enable the High Availability (HA) flag on the Cloud SQL instance.
Change the database character set to UTF-8.
correctAnswers: Create a Cloud SQL Read Replica and point the reporting tool to the replica.

explanation.general explanation: A Read Replica provides a read-only copy of the primary database. By offloading heavy analytical read queries to the replica, you eliminate resource contention on the primary instance, ensuring low latency for customer transactions while maintaining reporting performance.

why other options are wrong.Move the reporting tool to a different G: Moving the compute instance of the tool does not change the fact that it is querying the exact same primary database, so contention remains.
why other options are wrong.Enable the High Availability (HA) flag o: HA creates a standby replica for failover during outages. It cannot be used to serve read traffic and offload the primary database.
why other options are wrong.Change the database character set to UTF: Changing the character set has no significant impact on resolving query performance bottlenecks.

questions.questionText: Your team is running tightly coupled weather forecasting simulations on Compute Engine. The simulations require frequent inter-node communication, and any network latency significantly slows down the job. Which feature should you configure for these VM instances?

explanation.general explanation: A compact placement policy ensures that a group of virtual machine instances are located on the same or adjacent underlying physical hardware. This minimizes the physical distance between them, resulting in the lowest possible network latency for tightly coupled applications.

why other options are wrong.Spread placement policy: A spread placement policy places VMs on distinct physical hardware to maximize high availability. This would increase network latency, which is the opposite of the goal.
why other options are wrong.Preemptible VM instances: Preemptible VMs are short-lived, cheaper instances. They do not affect network latency.
why other options are wrong.Autohealing health checks: Autohealing restarts failed instances; it has no impact on network latency.

questions.questionText: A media company regularly transfers terabytes of video files between their on-premises data center and Google Cloud. They are currently using Cloud VPN over the public internet, but the latency is highly variable and throughput is insufficient. Which Google Cloud service provides a dedicated, highly reliable, and low-latency physical connection?

explanation.general explanation: Dedicated Interconnect provides a direct physical connection between your on-premises network and Google's network. Bypassing the public internet entirely ensures high throughput, consistent performance, and the lowest possible latency.

why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT: Cloud NAT allows internal Google Cloud instances to access the internet. It does not connect an on-premises data center to Google Cloud.
why other options are wrong.VPC Peering: VPC Peering connects two separate VPC networks within Google Cloud, not on-premises networks.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Router: Cloud Router facilitates dynamic BGP routing for VPNs and Interconnects, but on its own, it is a routing plane, not a physical low-latency connection product.

questions.questionText: A financial institution requires a fully managed relational database. To maintain a smooth user experience, the database must provide strong global consistency and low-latency reads for users scattered across three different continents. Which database service is specifically designed for this?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Spanner is Google Cloud's fully managed, horizontally scalable, relational database service. It is specifically designed to provide strong consistency and highly available, low-latency reads on a global scale.

why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL: Cloud SQL is a regional relational database. It cannot natively provide globally distributed strong consistency out-of-the-box.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Bigtable: Cloud Bigtable is a NoSQL wide-column database, not a relational database, and does not support standard SQL or relational constraints.
why other options are wrong.Firestore: Firestore is a NoSQL document database, not a relational database.

questions.questionText: Your data science team uses Looker to visualize massive datasets stored in BigQuery. Some complex dashboards take several seconds to load, frustrating the executive team. Which BigQuery feature should you enable to provide sub-second query response times for these dashboards?

explanation.general explanation: BigQuery BI Engine is a fast, in-memory analysis service built into BigQuery. It intelligently caches frequently accessed data in memory, allowing business intelligence (BI) tools like Looker to achieve sub-second query response times, drastically reducing dashboard latency.

why other options are wrong.BigQuery Data Transfer Service: This service automates data movement into BigQuery on a scheduled basis. It does not speed up query performance.
why other options are wrong.BigQuery ML: BigQuery ML allows you to build and execute machine learning models using standard SQL; it is not a performance caching layer.
why other options are wrong.BigQuery Omni: BigQuery Omni allows you to analyze data stored in AWS or Azure using BigQuery's interface. It does not improve local dashboard latency.

questions.questionText: You have deployed a serverless API using Cloud Run. Users report that if the API hasn't been accessed for an hour, the first request takes up to 5 seconds to respond, while subsequent requests respond in 50 milliseconds. How can you eliminate this initial latency?
options: Configure a minimum number of instances (min-instances) for the Cloud Run service.
Increase the memory limit allocated to the Cloud Run service.
Enable Cloud CDN in front of the Cloud Run service.
Change the HTTP method of the API from GET to POST.
correctAnswers: Configure a minimum number of instances (min-instances) for the Cloud Run service.

explanation.general explanation: The initial delay is known as a 'cold start', which occurs when Cloud Run spins up a new container instance from zero to handle a request. By configuring `min-instances` to 1 or more, Cloud Run keeps a container 'warm', completely eliminating cold start latency for new incoming traffic.

why other options are wrong.Increase the memory limit allocated to t: Adding memory might slightly speed up initialization, but it does not prevent the container from scaling down to zero and causing a cold start.
why other options are wrong.Enable Cloud CDN in front of the Cloud R: While CDN caches static content, dynamic API responses often cannot be cached, so the underlying cold start issue remains unresolved.
why other options are wrong.Change the HTTP method of the API from G: The HTTP method has absolutely no impact on serverless cold starts.

questions.questionText: You manage two separate Google Cloud projects with their own Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) networks. Services in Project A need to frequently communicate with services in Project B. To ensure the lowest possible network latency, how should you connect these VPCs?
options: Set up VPC Network Peering between the two VPCs.
Configure a Cloud VPN tunnel between the two VPCs over the public internet.
Assign external IP addresses to all instances and communicate via the internet.
Use Cloud NAT to route traffic from Project A to Project B.
correctAnswers: Set up VPC Network Peering between the two VPCs.

explanation.general explanation: VPC Network Peering enables direct private communication between two VPC networks in Google Cloud. Because traffic never leaves Google's internal network and uses private IPs, it provides the lowest possible latency and highest bandwidth without internet exposure.

why other options are wrong.Configure a Cloud VPN tunnel between the: VPN adds encryption overhead and requires gateways, introducing slight latency and bandwidth bottlenecks compared to native peering.
why other options are wrong.Assign external IP addresses to all inst: Routing traffic externally increases latency, uses public bandwidth, and severely degrades security.
why other options are wrong.Use Cloud NAT to route traffic from Proj: Cloud NAT is used for outbound internet access, not for low-latency internal communication between two VPCs.

questions.questionText: Your App Engine Standard application experiences occasional latency spikes when traffic suddenly increases, causing new instances to spin up to handle the load. How can you proactively reduce the latency associated with new instance initialization in App Engine?
options: Change the scaling configuration from automatic to manual.
Use a custom runtime with a larger Docker image.

explanation.general explanation: Warmup requests load your application code into a new instance before any live user requests reach that instance. This ensures that the application is fully initialized, thereby eliminating initialization latency (cold starts) for the end user.

why other options are wrong.Change the scaling configuration from au: Manual scaling requires you to pre-provision instances. While it stops cold starts, it eliminates auto-scaling benefits and increases costs drastically.
why other options are wrong.Use a custom runtime with a larger Docke: Larger images and custom runtimes (App Engine Flexible) typically take longer to initialize, increasing latency.
IAP is a security access control service and does not affect application scaling performance or startup latency.

questions.questionText: A MySQL database hosted on a Compute Engine instance is suffering from slow read/write performance. Cloud Monitoring shows that the 100 GB SSD Persistent Disk is hitting its maximum IOPS limit. You want to increase the IOPS performance without changing the disk type. What should you do?
options: Increase the size of the Persistent Disk to 500 GB.
Add a second 100 GB SSD Persistent Disk and use it for database backups.
Change the machine type to an n1-standard-1.
Format the disk with a different file system.
correctAnswers: Increase the size of the Persistent Disk to 500 GB.

explanation.general explanation: For standard and SSD Persistent Disks on Google Cloud, the maximum IOPS and throughput performance scales linearly with the size of the disk (up to the limits of the virtual machine). By simply increasing the disk capacity, you automatically provision higher IOPS and better latency performance.

why other options are wrong.Add a second 100 GB SSD Persistent Disk: Adding a second disk for backups does not increase the IOPS available to the primary disk serving the database traffic.
why other options are wrong.Change the machine type to an n1-standar: An n1-standard-1 is a small machine type and may actually lower maximum disk throughput limits rather than improve them.
why other options are wrong.Format the disk with a different file sy: File system changes will not overcome the fundamental IOPS limits established by the underlying Google Cloud storage layer based on disk size.

questions.questionText: You are creating a new Cloud Storage bucket to store financial reports that will only be accessed by the company's accounting team located exclusively in London. To ensure the lowest possible latency for these specific users, what bucket location type should you choose?
options: A Regional bucket located in the `europe-west2` (London) region.
A Dual-region bucket located in `europe-west1` and `europe-west4`.
correctAnswers: A Regional bucket located in the `europe-west2` (London) region.

explanation.general explanation: If all end-users accessing the data are physically located in a specific geographic area (like London), placing the data in a Regional bucket in that exact location provides the shortest network path and the lowest possible latency.

A multi-region bucket spans a large geographic area. While highly available, the data may be served from a data center further away than a dedicated regional bucket, leading to slightly higher latency.
why other options are wrong.A Dual-region bucket located in `europe-: Dual-region offers higher availability but does not guarantee the lowest latency for users exclusively in London compared to placing it directly in London (`europe-west2`).
why other options are wrong.A Regional bucket located in `us-central: Placing the bucket in the US for users in the UK would result in high transatlantic network latency.

questions.questionText: Users of your global application are complaining that the initial connection to your website is slow because the domain name resolution is taking over 500 milliseconds. Which Google Cloud service provides highly available and low-latency global domain name resolution?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud DNS is a scalable, reliable, and managed authoritative Domain Name System (DNS) service. It uses Google's global Anycast network to serve DNS zones from locations around the world, providing ultra-low latency domain name resolution to users everywhere.

why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT: Cloud NAT allows internal VM instances to securely access the internet; it has nothing to do with domain name resolution.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Domains: Cloud Domains is a domain registrar (where you purchase a domain name), not the fast, scalable DNS routing engine.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Endpoints: Cloud Endpoints is an API management system to secure, monitor, and analyze APIs, not a DNS resolution service.

questions.questionText: You want to improve the overall performance and reduce the latency of a web application fronted by an HTTP(S) Load Balancer and Cloud CDN. Which metric is the primary indicator of Cloud CDN's efficiency in reducing latency?

explanation.general explanation: The cache hit ratio represents the percentage of requests that are successfully served directly from the Cloud CDN edge cache without needing to fetch the data from the backend origin. A high cache hit ratio directly correlates with lower latency for end users.

why other options are wrong.Backend CPU utilization: While high CPU might cause latency, it does not measure the caching efficiency of the CDN itself.
why other options are wrong.Load balancer active connections: This measures traffic volume, not how effectively the CDN is caching data to reduce latency.
why other options are wrong.VPC network egress bytes: This is a billing and throughput metric, not a measurement of caching performance.

questions.questionText: Which two Google Cloud compute storage options provide the absolute highest Input/Output Operations Per Second (IOPS) and lowest latency for a Compute Engine virtual machine? (Select two)

explanation.general explanation: Local SSD offers the highest possible IOPS because it is physically attached to the host. If persistent network storage is required, Extreme Persistent Disk (pd-extreme) provides the highest IOPS and lowest latency among block storage options.

why other options are wrong.Standard Persistent Disk (pd-standard): Standard PDs use traditional Hard Disk Drives (HDDs) and have the lowest IOPS and highest latency among block storage options.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage Nearline: Nearline is an object storage class used for infrequent data access (backups), and has significantly higher latency and lower IOPS than any block storage.

questions.questionText: To dramatically improve performance and reduce latency, you decide to implement a caching strategy. Which two Google Cloud services are natively designed to act as high-speed caching layers? (Select two)

explanation.general explanation: Cloud CDN caches static web content at the network edge close to the user. Memorystore (for Redis or Memcached) provides in-memory data store caching for back-end applications to reduce database latency.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Source Repositories: This is a private Git repository service for hosting source code, not a caching service.
why other options are wrong.Cloud KMS: Cloud Key Management Service (KMS) manages cryptographic keys; it is a security service, not a caching layer.

questions.questionText: Your microservices on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) need to connect to a Cloud SQL database. To minimize network latency and improve security, how should you configure the connection between GKE and Cloud SQL?
options: Configure the Cloud SQL instance to use a Private IP within the same VPC network.
Assign a Public IP to Cloud SQL and route traffic over the public internet.
Set up an external VPN gateway to encrypt the database queries.
Place a Global Load Balancer in front of the Cloud SQL instance.
correctAnswers: Configure the Cloud SQL instance to use a Private IP within the same VPC network.

explanation.general explanation: Using a Private IP address for Cloud SQL ensures that all traffic between the GKE cluster and the database stays entirely within the internal Google Cloud network. This minimizes network hops, reduces latency, and enhances security by avoiding the public internet.

why other options are wrong.Assign a Public IP to Cloud SQL and rout: Routing traffic externally increases latency and exposes the database to potential internet-based security threats.
why other options are wrong.Set up an external VPN gateway to encryp: A VPN is unnecessary for services within the same Google Cloud VPC and would add encryption/decryption latency.
why other options are wrong.Place a Global Load Balancer in front of: Global Load Balancers manage HTTP(S) and TCP traffic for application frontends, not internal relational database connections.

questions.questionText: A gaming company requires a data processing pipeline that can ingest player actions, process them, and output results with the absolute minimum latency possible (real-time analytics). Which Google Cloud data processing service and mode should be used?
options: Cloud Dataproc running a nightly Hadoop job

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Dataflow in streaming mode processes data immediately as it arrives in a continuous stream. This architecture is designed specifically for real-time analytics and provides the lowest possible processing latency.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Dataflow in batch mode: Batch mode waits for a large collection of data to accumulate before processing it, inherently introducing significant latency.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Dataproc running a nightly Hadoop: A nightly job runs only once a day, meaning data could be up to 24 hours delayed, failing the real-time latency requirement.
why other options are wrong.BigQuery Data Transfer Service: This service moves data on a schedule; it is not a real-time data transformation and processing engine.

questions.questionText: You want to expose a static IP address to your users globally so they can access your web application. You want Google's network to ingest the user traffic as close to the user as possible to reduce latency. Which architectural pattern achieves this?
options: Reserve a Global static IP address and attach it to a Global External Application Load Balancer.
Reserve a Regional static IP address and attach it to a Compute Engine instance.
Use Cloud DNS to randomly rotate between multiple regional IP addresses.
Use a Regional External Application Load Balancer in the Premium Tier.
correctAnswers: Reserve a Global static IP address and attach it to a Global External Application Load Balancer.

explanation.general explanation: A Global External Application Load Balancer utilizes a single Global Anycast IP address. When combined with the Premium Network Tier, traffic enters Google's high-speed backbone at the edge location closest to the user, providing the lowest latency routing to your backends.

why other options are wrong.Reserve a Regional static IP address and: A regional IP means traffic must travel over the internet all the way to that specific region before entering Google's network, increasing latency for distant users.
why other options are wrong.Use Cloud DNS to randomly rotate between: DNS round-robin does not guarantee the user will hit the closest region, and doesn't utilize Anycast network ingestion.
why other options are wrong.Use a Regional External Application Load: A regional load balancer uses a regional IP address and cannot natively route traffic globally to multiple backends based on proximity.

questions.questionText: Your front-end application generates large HTML fragments that take significant CPU time to render. You want to cache these rendered fragments in memory to reduce page load latency. The cache does not need to be persistent, and data loss upon restart is acceptable. Which managed Google Cloud service is the best fit?

explanation.general explanation: Memorystore for Memcached provides a fully managed, high-performance, in-memory caching service. It is specifically designed for simple, fast caching of objects like HTML fragments where persistence and complex data types (like those in Redis) are not required.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage: Cloud Storage is an object storage service, not an in-memory cache. It has higher latency and is meant for persistent files.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Spanner: Cloud Spanner is a globally consistent relational database. Using it as a simple, non-persistent HTML cache is vastly over-engineered, expensive, and slower than in-memory Memcached.
why other options are wrong.Persistent Disk: Persistent Disk is block storage attached to VMs. Reading from disk is much slower than reading from an in-memory cache.

questions.questionText: You want to deploy Cloud CDN to reduce latency for your static assets. Which of the following Google Cloud resources can be configured as a valid backend origin for a Load Balancer serving Cloud CDN?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud CDN can be enabled on External Application Load Balancers. The valid backends for these load balancers (and thus Cloud CDN origins) include backend services (like Compute Engine MIGs, GKE, Cloud Run) and backend buckets (Cloud Storage).

why other options are wrong.A Cloud SQL instance: Cloud SQL is a database and cannot be placed directly behind an HTTP(S) Load Balancer as a web backend.
why other options are wrong.A Cloud Router: Cloud Router manages dynamic routing protocols (BGP); it does not serve web content.
why other options are wrong.A Memorystore instance: Memorystore is an internal in-memory cache accessed via private IP; it cannot be an origin for a public HTTP(S) Load Balancer.

questions.questionText: You are migrating a critical application and need to ensure the network latency between two specific Google Cloud regions is within acceptable limits before you deploy. Which native Google Cloud tool helps you visualize and measure the baseline latency between regions?

explanation.general explanation: The Performance Dashboard within the Network Intelligence Center provides visibility into the Google Cloud network's performance. It allows you to view historical and real-time packet loss and latency metrics between different Google Cloud regions and zones.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Trace: Cloud Trace is a distributed tracing system for applications (finding code/microservice bottlenecks), not for baseline physical network infrastructure latency between regions.
why other options are wrong.VPC Flow Logs: VPC Flow Logs record network traffic flows for security and billing analysis, but they do not provide a centralized dashboard of baseline inter-region network latency.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Profiler: Cloud Profiler analyzes CPU and memory utilization within the application code, not network latency.

questions.questionText: Which two Google Cloud database services provide multi-region configurations to enable local, low-latency reads for globally distributed users? (Select two)

explanation.general explanation: Both Cloud Spanner and Firestore offer true multi-region configurations. Data is automatically replicated globally, allowing users in different continents to perform reads with low latency from the region closest to them.

why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL: Cloud SQL is a regional service. While you can manually set up cross-region read replicas, it is not natively a globally distributed database in the way Spanner or Firestore is.
why other options are wrong.Memorystore for Memcached: Memorystore is a zonal/regional in-memory caching service, not a multi-region distributed database.

questions.questionText: Your team is running a compute-intensive video encoding application on Compute Engine. The processing time (latency) per video is too high. You need to upgrade the instances to a machine family specifically optimized for high-performance, CPU-bound workloads. Which machine family should you choose?

explanation.general explanation: Compute-optimized (C2 and C3) machine types offer the highest performance per core on Compute Engine. They are built for ultra-high performance, compute-bound workloads like video encoding, high-performance computing (HPC), and gaming servers.

why other options are wrong.Memory-optimized (M2): Memory-optimized machines are designed for workloads requiring massive amounts of RAM (like SAP HANA), not specifically for CPU-bound processing speed.
why other options are wrong.General-purpose (E2): General-purpose machines offer a balance of price and performance, but they do not provide the raw CPU clock speeds required for the fastest possible compute-bound execution.
why other options are wrong.Shared-core (e2-micro): Shared-core machines use a fraction of a CPU and are for low-traffic, bursty workloads. They would drastically increase video processing time.

questions.questionText: Which two statements correctly describe how Google Cloud's Premium Network Tier improves latency compared to the Standard Network Tier? (Select two)
options: Traffic enters Google's high-quality backbone network at an edge location closest to the end user.
Traffic travels primarily over Google's dedicated, uncongested global fiber network.
Traffic is compressed using advanced machine learning algorithms before leaving the region.
Traffic bypasses all firewalls and security checks to increase delivery speed.
correctAnswers: Traffic enters Google's high-quality backbone network at an edge location closest to the end user.
Traffic travels primarily over Google's dedicated, uncongested global fiber network.

explanation.general explanation: The Premium Tier improves performance by capturing user traffic at the edge point of presence (PoP) closest to them. Once ingested, the traffic travels over Google's private, reliable, and low-latency global fiber backbone rather than traversing the unpredictable public internet.

why other options are wrong.Traffic is compressed using advanced mac: The Premium Tier does not automatically apply ML compression to your traffic.
why other options are wrong.Traffic bypasses all firewalls and secur: Network security and firewalls (like Cloud Armor and VPC firewalls) are fully enforced regardless of the network tier used.

questions.questionText: A data analytics team is querying large, flat datasets stored in BigQuery. They notice that queries using `SELECT *` are taking longer and consuming significantly more resources than necessary. To improve query latency and reduce costs, what is the recommended BigQuery best practice?
options: Only query the specific columns needed by explicitly naming them in the SELECT statement.
Increase the network bandwidth limit for the project.
Export the data to a CSV file and open it in a spreadsheet application.
Change the BigQuery dataset location from a Multi-region to a Single region.
correctAnswers: Only query the specific columns needed by explicitly naming them in the SELECT statement.

explanation.general explanation: BigQuery uses a columnar storage architecture. Using `SELECT *` forces BigQuery to perform a full scan of every single column in the table, drastically increasing query latency and cost. Best practice is to explicitly select only the specific columns required.

why other options are wrong.Increase the network bandwidth limit for: BigQuery performance is managed internally by Google; you do not manually increase network bandwidth limits to speed up queries.
why other options are wrong.Export the data to a CSV file and open i: Exporting data is slower and spreadsheets cannot handle massive datasets, defeating the purpose of using an enterprise data warehouse.
why other options are wrong.Change the BigQuery dataset location fro: While dataset location affects compliance and availability, the root cause of the performance issue here is the inefficient `SELECT *` query pattern.
